2_Introduction: The performance parameters (PCE, open-circuit voltage (VOC), short-circuit current density (JSC) and fill factor (FF)) of the control PSCs are significantly improved (24.4758%, 1.1689 V, 25.196 mA/cm², and 83.1052%). Starting with a Cs0.05MA0.1FA0.85PbI3.0 solution at 1.65 mol/L, the base solution was formulated to form the core perovskite layer. For the perovskite deposition process, the perovskite solutions were deposited using a two-step spin-coating process at 1000 rpm for 5 s and 5500 rpm for 30 s. A timed antisolvent drop (150 µL at last 15 s) enhanced the perovskite crystallization kinetics. Next, the substrates were quickly transferred for annealing at 110 °C for 15 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁FA₀.₈₅PbI₃.₀ perovskite composition—featuring a mixed A-site cation ensemble—optimizes the Goldschmidt tolerance factor (~0.98) and octahedral distortion, thereby suppressing δ-phase formation while enhancing thermal and phase stability; the precise 1.65 mol/L precursor concentration, coupled with the two-step spin-coating protocol (1000 rpm/5 s for wet-film formation followed by 5500 rpm/30 s for rapid solvent expulsion), establishes controlled supersaturation and nucleation density, while the precisely timed antisolvent quench (150 µL at the 15 s mark) triggers instantaneous desolvation of PbI₂–DMSO–FA⁺ intermediates, accelerating the transition from solvated adducts to crystalline perovskite and minimizing unreacted PbI₂ residues and pinhole formation; this kinetic control directly suppresses undercoordinated Pb²⁺ and I⁻ vacancies at grain boundaries and surfaces, reducing non-radiative recombination centers and extending carrier lifetimes, as corroborated by high PL intensity and uniform spatial distribution in photoluminescence mapping—indicating homogeneous crystallization and low defect density across the film—and by XRD showing complete absence of the characteristic 12.6° PbI₂ peak alongside narrow (001) FAPbI₃ reflections (FWHM ≈ 0.12°) and suppressed (110)/(220) peak splitting, confirming high crystallinity, minimal microstrain, and phase-pure α-perovskite formation without 2D/δ-phase impurities; the subsequent 110 °C/15 min annealing further drives volatile byproduct removal and promotes grain coalescence, yielding large, densely packed grains with low-angle grain boundaries that facilitate efficient vertical charge transport and reduce interfacial trap-assisted recombination; collectively, these crystallization dynamics synergize with the intrinsic defect tolerance of the mixed-cation lattice—where FA⁺ stabilizes the cubic phase, MA⁺ enhances lattice flexibility, and Cs⁺ rigidifies the inorganic sublattice—to yield exceptional interfacial electronic quality, evidenced by uniform film coverage in optical microscopy and grayscale homogeneity in top-down imaging, which eliminates shunt pathways and ensures continuous charge extraction across the active area—ultimately delivering a PCE of 24.4758%, VOC of 1.1689 V, JSC of 25.196 mA/cm², and FF of 83.1052%.
